headline: NYC Mayor bans landlords from using AI images for property listings, requiring disclosure of digital alterations
summary: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani's "Rental Ripoff Report" targets deceptive landlord practices, including a new rule requiring disclosure of AI-generated or AI-edited property listing images.
details: NYC Mayor Zohran Mamdani has announced new measures to combat deceptive landlord practices, following a "Rental Ripoff Report." This comes shortly after a "click-to-cancel" rule aimed at other companies.

The report specifically recommends that landlords and realtors must disclose any use of AI to alter their property listings, including images. This aims to prevent properties from appearing more appealing than they are in reality.

Misleading AI-generated and AI-edited images are a growing problem in real estate, impacting tenants who sign leases remotely. The report emphasizes that tenants should not be deceived when reality doesn't match listing photos.

Mayor Mamdani stated that the report turns thousands of New Yorkers' stories of mold, pests, and unexplained fees into concrete action. He stressed that every New Yorker deserves a safe home and landlords will be held accountable.

Deputy Mayor for Housing and Planning, Leila Bozorg, added that these policies are rooted in real experiences and concerns. Cea Weaver, Director of the Mayor’s Office to Protect Tenants, highlighted the new chapter in tenant power.

The "Rental Ripoff Hearings," established by Mayor Mamdani, involved meeting with 2,400 New Yorkers across all five boroughs. Safety, living conditions, and deceptive landlord practices were key focuses of these discussions.

headline_marked: [[OpenAI repeatedly resets Codex usage limits]] for paid users
headline: OpenAI repeatedly resets Codex usage limits for paid users
summary: OpenAI frequently resets usage limits for its Codex and ChatGPT Work paid users, often announced via X. This allows continued exploration of the models despite rapid user growth and occasional system incidents.
details: OpenAI has been frequently resetting usage limits for its Codex and ChatGPT Work paid users. These resets, often announced unexpectedly by @thsottiaux on X, allow users to continue their work and exploration.
The company cites rapid user growth, reaching milestones like 7M, 8M, and 9M active users, as a primary reason for these resets. This helps manage system load while accommodating increasing demand.
Some resets are 'banked,' allowing users to apply them at their convenience via web, mobile, or desktop app. Other times, hard resets are issued, replenishing all limits immediately.

Occasional system incidents and reliability issues have also prompted resets. OpenAI has acknowledged these challenges, stating they are actively working to prevent recurrence and keep systems stable.

Despite the cost implications of these resets, OpenAI maintains 'good vibes' and encourages users to push the systems to their limits, even mentioning the exploration of GPT-5.6 Sol without a 5-hour rate limit at one point.
